categories.label: Addition & Support
categories.description: Add more points to strengthen your argument

connectors.usage: Furthermore, studies have shown that...
connectors.tip: Use at the start of a sentence to add a strong supporting point

connectors.usage: Moreover, the economic benefits are substantial.
connectors.tip: Slightly more formal than 'furthermore' — great for academic essays

connectors.usage: In addition to this, governments should consider...
connectors.tip: Safe and versatile — works in any essay type

connectors.usage: Additionally, the environmental impact cannot be ignored.
connectors.tip: Works well mid-paragraph to pile on evidence

connectors.usage: What is more, this approach has been proven effective.
connectors.tip: Adds emphasis — signals your next point is even stronger

connectors.usage: On top of that, the social consequences are severe.
connectors.tip: Slightly informal — best in Speaking Part 3 or less formal Task 2

connectors.usage: Not only does this reduce costs, but it also improves efficiency.
connectors.tip: Shows grammatical range — use inversion for Band 8+

connectors.usage: Coupled with rising inflation, unemployment poses a serious threat.
connectors.tip: Sophisticated connector — shows you can link ideas elegantly

categories.label: Contrast & Concession
categories.description: Show opposing ideas or acknowledge the other side

connectors.usage: However, this approach has significant drawbacks.
connectors.tip: The most common contrast connector — don't overuse it (max 2 per essay)

connectors.usage: Nevertheless, the benefits outweigh the disadvantages.
connectors.tip: Stronger than 'however' — signals you're dismissing a counterargument

connectors.usage: Nonetheless, this policy has achieved positive results.
connectors.tip: Interchangeable with 'nevertheless' — vary between them

connectors.usage: On the other hand, opponents argue that...
connectors.tip: Always pair with 'on the one hand' or a preceding point

connectors.usage: Conversely, rural areas have seen a decline in services.
connectors.tip: Shows a direct opposite — not just a different view

connectors.usage: In contrast to developed nations, developing countries face...
connectors.tip: Great for comparing two different situations or groups

connectors.usage: Although this has some merit, the overall impact is negative.
connectors.tip: Use to concede a point before making your main argument

connectors.usage: Despite the economic growth, inequality has widened.
connectors.tip: Follow with a noun/gerund, not a clause — 'despite + -ing'

connectors.usage: Whereas urban residents have access to healthcare, rural populations do not.
connectors.tip: Directly compares two contrasting situations in one sentence

connectors.usage: While it is true that technology creates jobs, it also displaces workers.
connectors.tip: Concession + counter — shows balanced thinking. Band 8 technique

connectors.usage: Admittedly, there are some drawbacks to this approach.
connectors.tip: Acknowledges the opposing view gracefully before countering it

connectors.usage: Having said that, the long-term benefits are clear.
connectors.tip: Transitions smoothly after conceding a point

connectors.usage: Therefore, it is essential that governments take action.
connectors.tip: Classic cause-effect connector — use for logical conclusions

connectors.usage: Consequently, many young people are unable to afford housing.
connectors.tip: More formal than 'so' — shows you understand academic register

connectors.usage: As a result of rapid urbanisation, traffic congestion has worsened.
connectors.tip: Can be used as 'as a result' or 'as a result of + noun'

connectors.usage: Thus, the correlation between education and income is well established.
connectors.tip: Short and punchy — great for concluding a chain of reasoning

connectors.usage: Hence, a more sustainable approach is needed.
connectors.tip: Slightly more formal than 'thus' — works well in conclusions

connectors.usage: This leads to a situation where inequality becomes entrenched.
connectors.tip: Shows a chain of consequences — good for problem/solution essays

connectors.usage: Owing to the lack of investment, public services have deteriorated.
connectors.tip: More sophisticated than 'because of' — use for variety

connectors.usage: This means that future generations will bear the consequences.
connectors.tip: Explains the implication of a point — very natural

connectors.usage: For this reason, early intervention programmes are crucial.
connectors.tip: Explicitly links back to the reason you just stated

connectors.usage: It follows that increased access to education reduces poverty.
connectors.tip: Shows logical deduction — very academic and impressive

categories.label: Examples & Evidence
categories.description: Support your points with specific examples

connectors.usage: For example, countries like Sweden have implemented...
connectors.tip: The standard — but try to vary with other phrases

connectors.usage: For instance, a recent study by WHO found that...
connectors.tip: Interchangeable with 'for example' — alternate between them

connectors.usage: Renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind power, are...
connectors.tip: Use mid-sentence to give quick examples within a list

connectors.usage: To illustrate this point, consider the case of Finland's education system.
connectors.tip: More sophisticated than 'for example' — shows deliberate structuring

connectors.usage: A case in point is the success of Singapore's public housing programme.
connectors.tip: Band 8 phrase — introduces a specific, detailed example

connectors.usage: This is evidenced by the sharp decline in literacy rates.
connectors.tip: Points to data or facts — adds academic weight

connectors.usage: As demonstrated by recent research, screen time affects sleep quality.
connectors.tip: References evidence without needing to cite a specific study

connectors.usage: One notable example is Japan's approach to elderly care.
connectors.tip: Signals you're about to give a strong, specific example

categories.label: Emphasis & Certainty
categories.description: Strengthen your position and stress key points

connectors.usage: Indeed, the evidence overwhelmingly supports this view.
connectors.tip: Reinforces a point — use after stating something strong

connectors.usage: In fact, the opposite is true.
connectors.tip: Use to correct a misconception or add surprising information

connectors.usage: Undoubtedly, education plays a crucial role in social mobility.
connectors.tip: Strong certainty — only use when the point is well-supported

connectors.usage: It is widely acknowledged that climate change poses a significant threat.
connectors.tip: Establishes consensus — good for opening arguments

connectors.usage: This is particularly evident in developing countries.
connectors.tip: Narrows focus to a specific area or group

connectors.usage: This is especially true for younger generations.
connectors.tip: Similar to 'particularly' — use to highlight a specific group

connectors.usage: It is worth noting that these results may vary across cultures.
connectors.tip: Draws attention to something the reader might overlook

connectors.usage: Significantly, this trend has accelerated in recent years.
connectors.tip: Signals the point is important for the overall argument

categories.label: Sequence & Organisation
categories.description: Structure your essay and guide the reader

connectors.usage: Firstly, it is important to consider the economic implications.
connectors.tip: Use for your first body paragraph — signals structure

connectors.usage: Secondly, the social impact must be examined.
connectors.tip: Don't go beyond 'thirdly' — it gets repetitive

connectors.usage: Finally, the environmental consequences deserve attention.
connectors.tip: Signals your last body point — not the conclusion

connectors.usage: To begin with, the main cause of this problem is...
connectors.tip: Alternative to 'firstly' — slightly less mechanical

connectors.usage: Following this logic, we can conclude that...
connectors.tip: Shows your ideas build on each other

connectors.usage: Subsequently, the government introduced new regulations.
connectors.tip: Shows chronological order — useful in process descriptions

connectors.word: Having considered X, it is also important to
connectors.usage: Having considered the economic factors, it is also important to examine the social implications.
connectors.tip: Band 8 transition — shows you're structuring deliberately

categories.label: Giving Opinions
categories.description: Express your view with appropriate hedging

connectors.usage: In my opinion, the advantages far outweigh the disadvantages.
connectors.tip: Direct and clear — use once in your essay, usually in the intro or conclusion

connectors.usage: I believe that governments should prioritise education spending.
connectors.tip: Personal and direct — fine for opinion essays

connectors.usage: From my perspective, this trend is largely positive.
connectors.tip: Slightly more sophisticated than 'I think'

connectors.usage: It seems to me that a balanced approach is needed.
connectors.tip: Softer opinion — good when you're not fully certain

connectors.usage: I am firmly convinced that education is the key to progress.
connectors.tip: Strong opinion — use in conclusion to restate your thesis

connectors.usage: It could be argued that technology has made life easier.
connectors.tip: Hedged — introduces a view without committing to it

connectors.usage: One could contend that stricter laws would reduce crime.
connectors.tip: Academic and distanced — shows sophistication

connectors.usage: I would argue that prevention is more effective than punishment.
connectors.tip: Confident but not aggressive — shows reasoned thinking

connectors.usage: In conclusion, the benefits of globalisation clearly outweigh the drawbacks.
connectors.tip: The standard conclusion opener — always safe

connectors.usage: To sum up, education reform requires a multi-faceted approach.
connectors.tip: Alternative to 'in conclusion' — slightly less formal

connectors.usage: Overall, the evidence suggests that early intervention is most effective.
connectors.tip: Great for Task 1 summaries and Task 2 conclusions

connectors.usage: All things considered, a balanced approach is the most sensible option.
connectors.tip: Shows you've weighed multiple factors — good for discussion essays

connectors.usage: Taking everything into account, it is clear that urgent action is needed.
connectors.tip: Longer but impressive — shows comprehensive thinking

connectors.usage: In light of the above arguments, I firmly believe that...
connectors.tip: Sophisticated — explicitly references your earlier arguments

connectors.usage: On balance, the advantages of remote work outweigh the disadvantages.
connectors.tip: Perfect for advantage/disadvantage essays — shows measured judgement
